title: EmberCare Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for EmberCare's Redwood onboarding. Covered contract scope (Dedicated vs Private), initial success criteria, timelines for sandbox and pilot, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and next steps to share access and run baseline benchmarks. Action items assigned for docs, infra checklist, and pilot dataset prep.
next_steps: Redwood to share onboarding deck and SLA summary
Customer to provision test VPC & VPN credentials
Schedule pilot benchmark run for week of 2027-11-21
Customer to provide sample dataset and redaction rules
action_items: Maya Chen: send onboarding deck, pricing summary, and SOC2 pointer by 2027-11-09
Rajiv Patel: prepare pilot benchmark plan and checklist by 2027-11-12
Sana Khan (EmberCare): share compliance questionnaire answers by 2027-11-10
Marcus Lee: provision VPC peering and test users by 2027-11-15
transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2027-11-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rajiv Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Redwood CSM); Olivia Park (EmberCare Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Eng Manager), Sana Khan (Security/Compliance), Tom Alvarez (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on onboarding plan and pilot scope.

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok everybody thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, so this is the embercare redwood onboarding kickoff. super excited to work with you all. first quick round of intros?
[00:18] Olivia Park: hi i'm olivia, head of ai at embercare, we're focused on clinical notes summarization and triage. excited to get the pilot running.
[00:27] Marcus Lee: hey team, marcus, engineering manager, i'll own infra and data work on our side.
[00:33] Sana Khan: sana from security and compliance, i'll be looking at the KMS and audit logs parts.
[00:39] Rajiv Patel: rajiv here, solutions eng at redwood, i'll be running the pilot benchmarks and helping with model configs.
[00:46] Aisha Gomez: aisha, csm, i'll coordinate timelines and onboarding tasks.
[00:52] Tom Alvarez: tom, product, focusing on success metrics for summarization quality.

[01:05] Maya Chen: good thanks. quick agenda: scope (dedicated vs private), success criteria, timeline, security checklist, and next steps. feel free to interrupt.

[01:22] Olivia Park: perfect. high level we want to compare: 1) hosted vs dedicated vs private; but leaning dedicated or private because of PHI concerns. initial immediate use is POC with de-identified data, then move to live with protected data.

[01:40] Rajiv Patel: that makes sense. for the pilot we usually recommend dedicated reserved capacity first — gives predictable latency and easier integration. private (vpc/on-prem) is possible but adds provisioning time.

[01:55] Marcus Lee: timeline is a constraint for us, we want results inside 3 weeks if possible — is that realistic?

[02:04] Rajiv Patel: three weeks is tight but doable for a focused pilot: week one for infra and access, week two for initial runs and tuning, week three for eval and handoff. if you need private deployment that adds a few weeks for network config and approvals.

[02:28] Sana Khan: on security, we require SOC2 type 2, SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS for keys, and audit logs retained for 90 days at minimum. are those supported?

[02:42] Maya Chen: yes we can support SAML/SSO and KMS integrations in private and dedicated. we have SOC2 reports and can share them, and audit logging is available via console. i'll attach the SOC2 docs after the call.

[03:00] Olivia Park: perfect. also curious about data residency — we need EU region handling for some data subsets, embercare has EU patients.

[03:08] Rajiv Patel: happy to route requests to eu region. for pilot we can spin up a eu-dedicated pool or use hosted region routing depending on your compliance needs.

[03:25] Tom Alvarez: success metrics: latency under 500ms p50 for single-request summarization, cost target <$0.01 per summary, and rouge/bleu-ish quality thresholds — we'll provide a few reference prompts.

[03:40] Rajiv Patel: sounds reasonable. we'll capture latency and token-level cost in the benchmark outputs. we typically run with a medium-sized 7B variant for faster TTR, and we can compare with a quantized 13B in a later iteration.

[03:56] Marcus Lee: quick Q on integrations: we'll need a webhook for results and a small SDK to call the route. do you provide sample code and npm package?
[04:05] Rajiv Patel: yes, we have SDKs (node/python) and example webhook flows. i'll drop a repo link in the follow-up. sometimes the transcript here said 'SDK' as 'S D K' but it's the normal packages.

[04:20] Maya Chen: ok let's walk through immediate onboarding tasks. first: access — we need an admin user for embercare in the console and service account credentials for the infra team. second: network — VPC peering or a site-to-site VPN depending on private vs dedicated. third: dataset prep and shared prompt set.

[04:40] Sana Khan: for service accounts we need least privilege and committed logs to our SIEM. can we forward audit logs to our Splunk?
[04:48] Rajiv Patel: yes log export options exist; we can push to S3 and you can pick them up, and for enterprise we have direct log forwarding integrations. i'll follow up with details.

[05:02] Olivia Park: about data de-id, our clinical team will create a de-identified sample set for the pilot, but we also want to trial with redaction rules that are applied before sending. is redwood able to run client-side redaction or do we need to do it upstream?
[05:18] Rajiv Patel: best practice is upstream redaction before calling the API, but we also offer a configurable pre-processing step in private deployments. we'll put options in the onboarding doc.

[05:35] Tom Alvarez: another question — how do rollbacks work in case a model regression occurs during rollout? we saw mention of canary and fallback.

[05:44] Maya Chen: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to the previous model or a smaller backed-up model if latency spikes or error rates exceed thresholds. the console shows per-route metrics so you can configure thresholds.

[06:00] Marcus Lee: cool. on billing — initial pilot will be on a usage invoice, but likely move to reserved capacity if we scale. what's the minimum for dedicated?

[06:12] Maya Chen: dedicated minimum is typically a monthly commit (varies by region/hw). i'll include the pricing sheet in the follow-up email.

[06:22] Olivia Park: ok good. lets talk timeline specifics. we agreed week of 2027-11-14 for sandbox access and week of 2027-11-21 for pilot runs?

[06:33] Aisha Gomez: yes i'll put a calendar invite for the sandbox handoff on 11/14 and a benchmark session on 11/22 to give a little buffer.

[06:40] Rajiv Patel: for the benchmark session i'll request the sample prompts and a 200-500 record sample. we'll run baseline against the curated 7B and a quantized 13B variant and produce latency/cost/quality matrix.

[06:56] Sana Khan: one security item — can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit for data in dedicated deployments?

[07:03] Rajiv Patel: yes encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS is supported for private/dedicated; in transit TLS is standard. again i'll include tech notes.

[07:15] Tom Alvarez: what's the expected RTO for support if we hit an incident during pilot?

[07:20] Maya Chen: for pilot customers we provide response in the business-hour SLA; for enterprise with premium SLAs we provide 24x7 support and tighter response times — i'll surface the SLA table.

[07:33] Olivia Park: great, last item — we'll need an internal stakeholder map so we know who to contact for costs/infra/security/product. i'll share that after the call.

[07:44] Maya Chen: perfect, that helps. any other blockers?

[07:48] Marcus Lee: none from eng, just need access details and network steps.
[07:52] Sana Khan: none aside from reviewing the SOC2 and KMS plan.

[07:58] Maya Chen: ok quick recap of next steps: i'll send onboarding deck, SOC2, and pricing; rajiv will send benchmark plan and SDK links; sana will send compliance answers; marcus to provision network. aisha will schedule the sandbox and benchmark calendar invites.

[08:20] Olivia Park: that all sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:26] Maya Chen: thanks team — we'll follow up by email with links. end of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: some auto-caption errors present (e.g., "K V cash" instead of "KV cache", "S D K" spaced). There were several short crosstalk spots around 03:40–04:10.
